title: Goyal Asks India, Egypt Startups to Co-Build Payments, Health Tech
excerpt: At the Egypt-India Startup Forum in Cairo, the commerce minister proposed cross-border payments built on UPI and InstaPay, plus joint work on water, farms and affordable medical devices.
body:
• Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal addressed the Egypt-India Startup Forum in Cairo on November 16, urging founders in both countries to build businesses that compete globally “from the Nile to the Ganga.”
  • Fintech leads the pitch: Goyal proposed co-building cross-border payment systems on India's UPI and Egypt's InstaPay, paired with recently launched local-currency trade.
  • He also named agriculture and water (precision irrigation, desalination, cold chains) and health tech (affordable diagnostics and medical devices for Africa and Asia) as joint work areas.
  • Goyal cited India's scale — nearly 250,000 registered startups across some 770 districts and more than 130 unicorns — and invited Egyptian founders to collaborate in India, saying an upcoming startup event had been moved up to January.

India's commerce minister used a startup forum in Cairo on Monday to ask founders in India and Egypt to stop thinking within their own borders. Addressing the Egypt-India Startup Forum, Piyush Goyal said startups in both countries need new markets, cross-border investment and partnerships to test and scale their ideas, and that putting the two ecosystems on a shared platform would turn innovation into shared prosperity, ANI reported.

“I would like to encourage all entrepreneurs to look beyond national boundaries, beyond our borders, bring together our strengths, create businesses that can compete globally from the Nile to the Ganga.”

— Piyush Goyal, Commerce and Industry Minister

Payments first: UPI meets InstaPay

Goyal pointed to fintech as the primary area for collaboration, saying India's Unified Payments Interface (UPI) and Egypt's InstaPay share a common vision. Co-building cross-border payment systems on that technology, paired with the local-currency trade the two countries have recently launched, would boost bilateral commerce and expand low-cost digital payments across Egypt, he said. “Together, we should not merely introduce our ecosystems; we should put them to work on a shared platform towards the future,” the minister said.

Water, farms and affordable health tech

Beyond payments, Goyal named agriculture, water management, healthcare and heritage tourism as avenues for joint innovation. Startups from both countries could co-create precision irrigation, desalination and cold-chain solutions to manage scarce water, he suggested. In health tech and pharmaceuticals, he proposed developing affordable diagnostics and medical devices to serve not only India and Egypt but the wider regions of Africa and Asia. “The real strength of startups is not measured only by the number of unicorns or the total number of startups it produces. It is measured by its ability to solve problems, create employment, improve lives, and delve into solutions that can serve the world,” he added.

He also urged entrepreneurs to use augmented reality, virtual reality and smart travel portals to bring monuments such as the Egyptian pyramids and the Taj Mahal to life, and stressed building green hydrogen, quantum computing and artificial intelligence technologies in languages such as Arabic, Hindi, Tamil and Marathi for the Global South. Tracing trade between the two countries back thousands of years, he cited the roughly 1,800-year-old Muziris Papyrus, which recorded a shipping loan between Kerala and Alexandria.

The visit around the forum

The forum sat inside a two-day official visit on November 15–16. Goyal co-chaired the 7th India-Egypt Joint Trade Committee meeting with Egypt's Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade, Dr. Mohamed Farid Saleh, and travelled with a delegation of more than 130 business leaders and startups, according to the Press Information Bureau. Detailing India's growth under the Startup India initiative, Goyal said the country has become what he described as the world's third-largest startup ecosystem, with nearly 250,000 registered startups across about 770 districts, over 130 unicorns, and 48 per cent of ventures featuring at least one woman director or co-founder. Bilateral trade between India and Egypt was $6.5 billion in FY 2025-26; our earlier coverage of the visit sets out the trade numbers and the wider partnership push.

What happens next

Goyal invited Egyptian founders to collaborate in India and said the date of an upcoming startup event had been moved up to January; the ANI report did not name the event or give a date. For founders, the concrete opening from Monday's forum is the payments proposal: a UPI-InstaPay build would need the two countries' fintechs and regulators to do the co-creation Goyal described, and no timeline for it was announced at the forum.
